title: A Dimension-Agnostic Bootstrap Anderson-Rubin Test For Instrumental Variable Regressions
abstract: arXiv:2412.01603v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Weak-identification-robust tests for instrumental variable (IV) regressions are typically developed separately depending on whether the number of IVs is treated as fixed or increasing with the sample size, forcing researchers to make a stance on the asymptotic behavior, which is often ambiguous in practice. This paper proposes a bootstrap-based, dimension-agnostic Anderson-Rubin (AR) test that achieves correct asymptotic size regardless of whether the number of IVs is fixed or diverging, and even accommodates cases where the number of IVs exceeds the sample size. By incorporating ridge regularization, our approach reduces the effective rank of the projection matrix and yields regimes where the limiting distribution of the AR statistic can be a weighted chi-squared, a normal, or a mixture of the two. translated_abstract: 针对工具变量（IV）回归的弱识别稳健检验，通常根据工具变量数量被视为固定还是随样本量增加而分别开发，这迫使研究者必须对渐近行为表明立场，而这种渐近行为在实践中往往是模糊不清的。本文提出了一种基于自助法（bootstrap）的、维度无关的Anderson-Rubin（AR）检验，无论工具变量数量是固定还是发散，该检验都能实现正确的渐近水平（size），甚至可以适用于工具变量数量超过样本量的情形。通过引入岭（ridge）正则化，我们的方法降低了投影矩阵的有效秩，并由此产生了AR统计量极限分布可以是加权卡方分布、正态分布或两者混合的不同情形。强近似结果确保了自助法程序在所有情形下均保持一致有效，同时还提供了subst
tldr: 本文提出了一种基于自助法的维度无关Anderson-Rubin检验，通过岭正则化，无论工具变量数量固定、发散甚至超过样本量，都能保证检验具有正确的渐近水平和一致有效性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a bootstrap-based, dimension-agnostic Anderson-Rubin test for IV regressions that maintains correct asymptotic size whether the number of instruments is fixed, diverging, or even exceeds the sample size, by incorporating ridge regularization.
